eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 28 · Joining Tables

eyebrow: Chaining JOINs — four tables at once
code:
SELECT soh.OrderDate, p.Name, sod.OrderQty,
       per.FirstName, per.LastName
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS soh
INNER JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
    ON soh.SalesOrderID = sod.SalesOrderID
INNER JOIN Production.Product AS p
    ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID
INNER JOIN Person.Person AS per
    ON soh.CustomerID = per.BusinessEntityID;
caption: Each JOIN connects to whatever's already available — not always the first table.

code:
SELECT p.Name, sod.OrderQty
FROM Production.Product AS p
LEFT JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
    ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID
INNER JOIN Production.ProductSubcategory AS ps
    ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID;
caption: Keeps every product (LEFT), but requires a valid subcategory (INNER) — in one query.

subtitle: Joining to a table-valued function instead of a table.
